ideas.text: Knowledge is virtue; ignorance is the source of evil
The unexamined life is not worth living
True knowledge comes from recognizing one's own ignorance
The soul is immortal and distinct from the body
The Theory of Forms: true reality consists of eternal, abstract Forms
Knowledge is recollection of what the soul knew before birth
The ideal state is ruled by philosopher-kings
The soul has three parts: reason, spirit, and appetite
Justice is harmony between the parts of the soul and state
Form and matter are inseparable; universals exist in particular things
Knowledge comes through sensory experience and induction
Eudaimonia (flourishing) is the highest good, achieved through virtue
Virtue is a mean between excess and deficiency
Man is by nature a political animal
Logic is the tool of all sciences; syllogistic reasoning
Pleasure (ataraxia) is the highest good and goal of life
The gods do not intervene in human affairs
Death is nothing to us; when we exist, death is absent
Reality consists of atoms and void
Live according to nature and reason; virtue is the only good
We are all citizens of a universal community bound by reason
External things cannot harm the inner self; only our judgments do
God is the source of all truth; illumination of the mind by God
Evil is the privation of good, not a substance in itself
Free will exists but is corrupted by original sin
Time exists only in the mind, not objectively
Faith and reason are complementary paths to truth
Five Ways: cosmological arguments for God's existence
Natural law is grounded in divine reason and accessible to all
Being is the fundamental concept; essence and existence are distinct
Cogito ergo sum: 'I think, therefore I am' — the foundation of certainty
Mind-body dualism: mind and body are distinct substances
Clear and distinct ideas perceived by reason are true
The ontological argument: God's essence entails existence
God and Nature are identical; there is only one substance (pantheism)
Mind and body are two aspects of the same substance
Freedom is acting in accordance with one's own nature and reason
Adequate ideas (rational knowledge) lead to freedom and blessedness
The mind is a tabula rasa; all knowledge comes from experience
People have natural rights: life, liberty, and property
Government authority is derived from the consent of the governed
Primary qualities (shape, motion) are in objects; secondary qualities (color, taste) are in perceivers
Reality consists of monads: simple, indivisible, spiritual substances
This is the best of all possible worlds; God chose the world with maximum perfection
Pre-established harmony: mind and body do not interact but are synchronized by God
Innate ideas: the mind is not blank but contains truths from reason
All knowledge derives from impressions and ideas; nothing comes from pure reason
Causation is a habit of the mind, not a necessary connection in nature
The self is a bundle of perceptions, not a unified substance
Moral judgments are based on sentiment, not reason
Induction cannot be rationally justified (the problem of induction)
Man is naturally good; society and civilization corrupt him
The Social Contract: legitimate authority requires the general will
Natural inequality is acceptable; social inequality of power is not
The mind actively structures experience; space, time, and categories are a priori
Things-in-themselves (noumena) are unknowable; we only know phenomena
The Categorical Imperative: act only according to maxims you could will to be universal laws
Moral worth comes from acting from duty, not inclination or consequences
Humans are ends in themselves, never merely means
Reality is the unfolding of Absolute Spirit (Geist) through dialectical process
Dialectic: thesis → antithesis → synthesis is the logic of reality and history
Freedom is realized through ethical life (family, civil society, state)
Self-consciousness requires recognition by another consciousness
History is driven by class struggle and material (economic) forces
Capitalism alienates workers from their labor and their humanity
Ideology is the superstructure that legitimizes the economic base
The goal is a classless communist society where each contributes and receives freely
Utilitarianism: the right act maximizes overall happiness (utility)
Higher pleasures (intellectual) are qualitatively superior to lower pleasures
The Harm Principle: liberty should only be restricted to prevent harm to others
Inductive reasoning is the basis of scientific knowledge
'God is dead': the collapse of absolute moral values in modernity
Will to Power: the fundamental drive of all living beings
Eternal Recurrence: the supreme test — would you will to live this life again?
The Übermensch creates new values beyond slave morality
Slave morality (good/evil) arose from resentment against the noble morality
Logic is the foundation of mathematics; arithmetic is reducible to logic (logicism)
Sense and reference: two words can have the same referent but different senses
Thoughts (propositions) are objective, abstract entities, not mental states
Logical atomism: the world consists of atomic facts mirrored by propositions
Knowledge by acquaintance vs. knowledge by description
The theory of definite descriptions: 'The F is G' analyzed as a quantified formula
Mathematics is reducible to logic (logicism)
Early: The world is the totality of facts; language pictures the world
Early: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent
Later: Meaning is use in a language-game embedded in a form of life
Later: Philosophy therapy — dissolve rather than solve philosophical problems
Private language is impossible; language requires public criteria
Being-in-the-world: Dasein is always already embedded in a world of meaning
Being-toward-death: authentic existence requires confronting one's mortality
The question of Being has been forgotten by Western metaphysics
Technology discloses the world as a resource to be ordered and stored
Existence precedes essence: we have no predetermined nature or purpose
Radical freedom: we are 'condemned to be free'; our choices define us
Bad faith: self-deception about one's freedom and responsibility
Hell is other people: conflict is constitutive of human relations
Falsifiability is the criterion of scientific theories; science progresses through conjectures and refutations
Induction is invalid; we cannot verify scientific laws, only falsify them
The Open Society opposes totalitarianism and historicist grand theories
Critical rationalism: hold beliefs provisionally and remain open to revision
Science progresses through paradigm shifts, not continuous accumulation
Normal science works within a paradigm; crises lead to scientific revolutions
Paradigms are incommensurable: scientists in different paradigms inhabit different worlds
Justice as fairness: principles of justice chosen from behind a veil of ignorance
The Difference Principle: inequalities are just only if they benefit the least advantaged
Reflective equilibrium: balance moral intuitions with theoretical principles
